\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সম্পর্ক} (sômpôrkô)}{সম্পর্ক (sômpôrkô)}]{\bn{সম্পর্ক} (sômpôrkô) — a relationship; a connection}

\label{lesson:BN-C487-somporko}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to put to sleep, then the Bengali for to crawl.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সম্পর্ক}}
\textbf{\bn{সম্পর্ক}} — \emph{sômpôrkô} — \textquotedblleft{}a relationship; a connection\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দুই} \bn{ভাইয়ের} \bn{সম্পর্ক} \bn{ভালো।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dui bhāiyer sômpôrkô bhālo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The two brothers get on well.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সম্পর্ক}} (\emph{sômpôrkô}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{samparka}, \textquotedblleft{}mixing together, union, contact\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sômpôrkô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sômpôrkô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dui bhāiyer sômpôrkô bhālo.} — The two brothers get on well.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to put to sleep, then the Bengali for to crawl, then say \emph{sômpôrkô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{সম্পর্ক} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A relationship; a connection\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{কোল} (kol)}{কোল (kol)}]{\bn{কোল} (kol) — a lap}

\label{lesson:BN-C487-kol}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to crawl, then the Bengali for a relationship.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{কোল}}
\textbf{\bn{কোল}} — \emph{kol} — \textquotedblleft{}a lap\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{শিশুটা} \bn{দিদিমার} \bn{কোলে} \bn{বসে} \bn{আছে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shishuṭā didimār kole bôse āchhe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The child is sitting on its grandmother's lap.
\end{quote}

\bn{কোলে} \bn{নেওয়া}, to take onto your lap, to pick up a child.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{কোল}} (\emph{kol}) is listed by CDIAL for Bengali under Sanskrit \emph{krōḍa}, \textquotedblleft{}breast, bosom\textquotedblright{}, with its side form \emph{kōla}, \textquotedblleft{}lap\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 3607).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kol}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shishuṭā didimār kole bôse āchhe.} — The child is sitting on its grandmother's lap.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to crawl, then the Bengali for a relationship, then say \emph{kol} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ছোঁয়া} (chhõyā)}{ছোঁয়া (chhõyā)}]{\bn{ছোঁয়া} (chhõyā) — to touch}

\label{lesson:BN-C487-chhoya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a relationship, then the Bengali for a lap.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ছোঁয়া}}
\textbf{\bn{ছোঁয়া}} — \emph{chhõyā} — \textquotedblleft{}to touch\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বাচ্চাটা} \bn{গরম} \bn{কেটলিটা} \bn{ছুঁল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bāchchāṭā gôrôm keṭliṭā chhũlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The child touched the hot kettle.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{শিশুর} \bn{মাথা} \bn{ছুঁলেন}, \emph{tini shishur māthā chhũlen}.

As a noun, a touch: \bn{মায়ের} \bn{ছোঁয়া}, a mother's touch.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ছোঁয়া}} (\emph{chhõyā}) is listed by CDIAL for Bengali under Sanskrit \emph{chupati}, \textquotedblleft{}touches\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 5055); \bn{ছোঁয়াচে}, contagious, is built on it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chhõyā}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a relationship, then the Bengali for a lap, then say \emph{chhõyā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{আগলানো} (āglāno)}{আগলানো (āglāno)}]{\bn{আগলানো} (āglāno) — to shelter; to guard protectively}

\label{lesson:BN-C487-aglano}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a lap, then the Bengali for to touch.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{আগলানো}}
\textbf{\bn{আগলানো}} — \emph{āglāno} — \textquotedblleft{}to shelter; to guard protectively\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{মুরগিটা} \bn{বাচ্চাদের} \bn{আগলে} \bn{রাখল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{murgiṭā bāchchāder āgle rākhlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The hen kept her chicks sheltered.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{নাতিকে} \bn{আগলে} \bn{রাখলেন}, \emph{tini nātike āgle rākhlen}.

Usually with \bn{রাখা}: \bn{আগলে} \bn{রাখা}, to keep sheltered.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{আগলানো}} (\emph{āglāno}) is a Bengali verb for keeping someone safe inside your guard; its origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বোলানো} (bolāno)}{বোলানো (bolāno)}]{\bn{বোলানো} (bolāno) — to run (a hand) over; to stroke}

\label{lesson:BN-C487-bolano}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to touch, then the Bengali for to guard protectively.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বোলানো}}
\textbf{\bn{বোলানো}} — \emph{bolāno} — \textquotedblleft{}to run (a hand) over; to stroke\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দিদিমা} \bn{নাতির} \bn{মাথায়} \bn{হাত} \bn{বোলালেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{didimā nātir māthāy hāt bolālen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Grandmother stroked her grandson's head.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{কুকুরটার} \bn{পিঠে} \bn{হাত} \bn{বোলালেন}, \emph{tini kukurṭār piṭhe hāt bolālen}.

Its object is the hand: \bn{মাথায়} \bn{হাত} \bn{বোলানো}, to stroke someone's head.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বোলানো}} (\emph{bolāno}) is a Bengali verb for passing the hand gently over something; its origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bolāno}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to touch, then the Bengali for to guard protectively, then say \emph{bolāno} again
\end{itemize}
